headline: US voters reject AI data centers
dek: Restrictions passed in at least ten states in the November 3 elections, per CNBC.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The ballot box says no
body: Voters in at least ten states approved limits on AI data centers, per CNBC and Engadget.
Of the local votes, only Harwood, North Dakota, rejected the restriction.

points.t: Sherrod Brown beat Jon Husted, the face of data centers.
Gina Hinojosa beat Greg Abbott and backs a moratorium.
Keisha Lance Bottoms won, per Wired.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: The issue mattered
body: In an NBC News poll, 56% of voters said data centers and AI were an important factor (CNBC).
Greg Casar called the backlash the first tremor of a bigger AI earthquake, per Wired.

stat.cap: say AI mattered to their vote, says CNBC

items.t: Which builds get delayed is still undecided.

caption.hook: Voters in at least ten US states approved limits on AI data centers in the elections.
body: Per CNBC and Engadget, of the local votes on the issue only Harwood, North Dakota, rejected the restriction. In Ohio, Sherrod Brown beat Jon Husted, whom he called the face of data centers, and in Texas Gina Hinojosa beat Greg Abbott.

An NBC News poll cited by CNBC shows 56% of voters saw data centers and AI as an important factor. Projects by OpenAI, SoftBank and Nvidia depend on local approval, and which ones get delayed is not yet decided.
